svg.title: Transactional outbox
svg.desc: Save the event in the same transaction as the data; a relay publishes it later. The database write is one transaction inserting both the order row and the outbox row; it is drawn as a single write token. The relay is shown polling; log-tailing (CDC) relays behave the same way. Delivery is at-least-once: a relay that crashes after publishing but before marking the row sent will publish it again, so consumers must be idempotent. 1. Atomic write: order and event commit together or not at all. 2. Relay publishes: the relay reads the row, publishes it, then marks it sent. 3. Broker down: orders still commit; their events wait in the outbox. 4. Backlog drains: the broker recovers and the relay publishes every waiting event.
